playas.descripcion: The beach is located within the bay bearing the same name and is very close to the Port of Portbou. It is bounded by a stretch of rocks to the north, where we find some small coves, and by the jetty and the paved path leading to the wharf to the south.
The beach is bounded by a stretch of rocks to the north and by Les Portes Beach and the Port of Colera to the south.

The beach is part of the L'Albrera Natural Site of National Interest. It receives many visitors because of its natural beauty and because of its proximity to the main road, which provides easy access.
The beach is bounded by two stretches of rocks to the north and the south. It can be found 1000 m north of the Port of Llancà.
The beach is bounded by the mouth of the Valleta Stream to the north and by the jetty of the Port of Llancà to the south, which protects it from the open sea.
The beach is part of a stretch of rocky coastline with small coves. To the south we find Les Tonyines Beach.
The beach is part of a stretch of rocky coastline with small coves. This is a fairly secluded beach protected from the open sea by the rocky stretches found to the north and south.

playas.nombre: El Port de la Vall Beach
playas.descripcion: The beach is part of a stretch of rocky coastline with small coves.

playas.nombre: El Port de la Selva Beach
playas.descripcion: The beach is located in the bay of El Port de la Selva and is protected from the open sea. It is located at the southern end of the port.
This is a small beach, located within the centre of the town and close to the jetty found at the port. It is bounded by two stretches of rocks to the north and south.
The beach is protected from the open sea by the bay in which it is located and it represents the northern boundary of Cap de Creus Natural Park.

The beach can be found in a little nook off the irregular coastline of Cape Creus, away from the centre and bounded by two stretches of rocks to the north and south. It is very close to Cap de Creus Natural Park.

The beach is located within the centre of the town, in the bay that protects it from the open sea where many boats are moored. Some Art Nouveau houses can be found along the promenade. It is very close to Cap de Creus Natural Park.
The beach is located outside the town centre and is part of a stretch of coastline which boasts a number of coves and small beaches. It is very close to Cap de Creus Natural Park.

A spacious cove, ideal refuge for boats and for doing a spot of diving. It can be found at the southern end of Cap de Creus Natural Park and is bounded by two stretches of rocks and cliffs to the north and south.

The water at this beach is of an intense blue colour and the spot offers refuge from the tramuntana, or northerly wind. It is located in the residential housing development that bears the same name, bounded by a stretch of rocks to the southeast and by the cliffs of the development to the northeast.

The beach has golden sand and transparent, sandy-bottomed waters, which are loved by swimmers enjoying protection from the tramuntana, or northerly wind. It is located in the residential housing development of the same name, bounded by two stretches of rocks to the north and south.

This is a beach with clear waters and rocky, sandy bottoms. It is a favourite spot among the inhabitants of Roses, who also call it El Segon Moll Beach. It is bounded by a stretch of rocks to the southeast and by the breakwater of the Port of Roses to the northwest.

The beach is located in the Roses town centre and has fine sand and deep, transparent waters that are ideal for families and for practising all kinds of water sports. It is located between the Port of Roses and one of the breakwaters that channel the mouth of the Ginjolers Stream.

Beach located at the heart of Roses, with fine sand and shallow water that goes from the breakwater at Riera Ginjolers until the Bruneta stream, which separates it from Salatar Beach. Behind it is the Passeig Marítim promenade with views of the Bay of Roses.

Beach that extends from the mouth of the Bruneta stream to the Santa Margarida residential marina. The residential marina is an important tourist area, with more than 15 km of navigable canals. At the southern end of the beach there is a square with benches and vegetation, overlooking the Aiguamolls de l' Empordà.

The beach is inside Els Aiguamolls de l'Empordà Natural Park. It is home to a unique and fragile ecosystem due to the strict conditions under which its flora and fauna live. It is bounded by two important tourist areas: Santa Margarida (Roses) to the northeast, separated by the outlet of the residential marina, and Empuriabrava to the southwest, separated by the Madral channel.

It is a tourist beach with fine sand, located in the Empuriabrava residential community, built upon a wetland area, which is why there are a lot of canals. It is bordered on the northeast with the Empuriabrava marina, and on the southwest, with the mouth of the Muga river.

This is a beach bounded by the mouths of the Fluvià River and the Muga River. Most of this beach is located within Les Llacunes Full Natural Reserve of Els Aiguamolls de l'empordà Natural Park. It is especially well-known for its dunes, as well as the large number of lagoons that dominate the landscape and which are particularly important for the vegetation and different bird communities that live there. The beach is closed to the public during nesting season, given the presence of such vulnerable species as the Kentish plover (Charadrius alexandrinus).

playas.nombre: de Can Sopa- la Gola Beach
playas.descripcion: It is a part of the extensive Sant Pere Pescador beach, which is over 6 km long. It is located in a Special Protection Area of Biological and Scenic Importance, part of the Aiguamolls de l'Empordà Natural Park, extending across sand dunes and Mediterranean vegetation.  The Fluvià River flows into the sea here. Ideal for sports like windsurfing and sailing, due to its moderate winds.

playas.nombre: cal Cristià - Cortal de la Vila Beach
playas.descripcion: A section of beach that is part of the extensive, uninterrupted beach of Sant Pere Pescador, over 6 km long, surrounded by areas of particular biological and scenic importance at the mouth of the Fluvià river, in the middle of the Bay of Roses. It extends across sand dunes and Mediterranean vegetation, between the section of Can Sopa and Cortal de la Devesa. Ideal for sports like windsurfing and sailing, due to its moderate thermal winds.

playas.nombre: El Cortal de la Devesa Beach
playas.descripcion: A section that is part of the extensive, uninterrupted beach of Sant Pere Pescador, surrounded by areas of particular biological and scenic importance at the mouth of the Fluvià river, in the middle of the Bay of Roses. It extends across sand dunes and Mediterranean vegetation, between Cal Cristià and the Riuet beach. Ideal for sports like windsurfing and sailing, due to its moderate thermal winds. It has over 200 meters of space available for kitesurfing.

It is bounded by a breakwater known as Punta de Sant Martí to the north and Les Muscleres Beach to the south. The remains of a port from the Hellenistic period are conserved here, and behind the beach we find the Greco-Roman archaeological site of Empúries, which dates back to between the 6th century BC and the 3rd century AD.

It is bounded by El Moll Grec Beach to the north (where we find the remains of a Hellenistic port) and by a stretch of rocks to the south. Behind the beach we find the Greco-Roman archaeological site of Empúries, which dates back to between the 6th century BC and the 3rd century AD. A pine grove runs along the beach close to the sea.
The beach can be found just outside the town of l'escala and is bounded by a stretch of rocks to the north and the mouth of the El Molí canal to the south.
This is a very small, family beach in the centre of town, which is bounded to the west by a stretch of rocks and by a jetty to the east.

The fine sand and shallow waters of this beach make it ideal for children. It is located in the town centre of l'escala and is protected from the open sea by the bay. It is bounded by a promenade to the northwest and by the Port of l'escala to the northeast.

It is found at the border between l'escala and Torroella de Montgrí. The protected area of the Montgrí massif starts at its southern end. Its location helps to protect this cove from the tramuntana, or northerly wind.

It is part of the Montgrí, Medes Islands and Baix Ter Natural Park. It is confined in the north by the port of L¿Estartit and in the south by the mouth of the Ter River and the beach known as Fonollera or Mas Pinell.

It is part of El Montgrí, les Illes Medes i el Baix Ter Natural Park and is located in a semi-natural environment made up of dunes and meadows. It is bounded by the mouth of the Ter River to the north and by El Grau Beach, in Pals, to the south, where we find the mouth of the El Molí canal (Pals).

The coastal area of Pals boasts one of the Costa Brava¿s longest and most spectacular beaches. This beach, which is formed by dunes and pines, affords some magnificent views of the Medes Islands. Grau beach borders on La Fonollera or Mas Pinell beach (Torroella de Montgrí) in the north and, in the south, is adjacent to the main beach of Pals. The Molí irrigation channel and Les Basses d¿en Coll wetlands join the sea at the same point on the beach.

The coastal area of Pals has one of the longest and most spectacular beaches on the Costa Brava. With its dunes and pine trees, this beach enjoys fantastic views of the Medes Islands. It is bounded by El Grau Beach, Pals, to the north and by El Racó Beach (Begur) to the south.

This is the southernmost part of the long stretch of coastline of the Bay of Pals and is bounded by Platja Gran Beach, Pals, to the north and by a stretch of rocks to the south, where we find a path taking us to Illa Roja Beach.

It is bounded by a small stretch of rocks to the north, which continues towards El Racó Beach, and by an area of cliffs to the south, which is the beginning of the Les Muntanyes de Begur Area of Natural Interest.

It is found in the midst of the rocky stretch of coast of the Les Muntanyes de Begur Area of Natural Interest, among stretches of rocks and cliffs. It is one of the largest beaches in Begur and the closest to the town centre, enjoying a privileged location, with the Cala des Port des Pi situated to its right and Cala del Rei to its left. This beach maintains a traditional air and offers different sporting activities and tourism facilities. Its name comes from a torrent that divides the beach in two.
It is found in the midst of the rocky stretch of coast in the Les Muntanyes de Begur Area of Natural Interest, among crags and cliffs.

It is found in the midst of the rocky stretch of coast in the Les Muntanyes de Begur Area of Natural Interest, among crags and cliffs. It is located right at the foot of the imposing Cape Begur. With its coarse, dark sand, this natural hideaway has managed to remain untouched and to retain a primitive purity that is rarely found elsewhere on the Costa Brava.

It is found in the midst of the rocky stretch of coast in the Les Muntanyes de Begur Area of Natural Interest, among crags and cliffs. At the water's edge, views of the majestic cliff of Cape Begur can be enjoyed to the north.

The beach can be found at the centre of the bay bearing the same name and at the southern side of the Les Muntanyes de Begur Area of Natural Interest. This is an old fishing village that has now become a popular summer destination. A seaside path leads to Llafranc Beach, taking in the Sant Sebastià mountain.

This beach, which is flanked by cliffs, is in the Bay of Llafranc, in front of an old fishing village bearing the same name. A small port can be found at the eastern side, where we also find the start of the seaside path that takes us to Tamariu Beach, taking in the Sant Sebastià lighthouse, atop the Sant Sebastià mountain. Another path can be found to the west of the beach, which leads to Calella and is shorter and more leisurely than the previous one. The Sant Sebastià mountain protects the beach when the tramuntana, or northerly wind, is strong.

It is the largest beach in the centre of Calella de Palafrugell, which used to be a fishing village. The beach is flanked by a promenade lined with stately summer homes from the first half of the last century. West of the beach, on the Punta del Conill, we find a characteristic, pink-coloured house which boasts great views of the area. A seaside path that starts in Port Bo takes us to Llafranc, snaking by the coastline just metres from the sea.

The beach can be found in the centre of Calella de Palafrugell, which used to be a fishing village. It is located practically in front of Les Voltes, a series of arches built in the 19th century, behind which runs a covered walkway. Many events are held in the small square next to it, such as sardana dancing on Saturday evenings in summer, and the popular habanera singing festival held on the first Saturday in July. A seaside path links this beach with the one in Llafranc, running along the coastline just a few metres from the sea.

The beach can be found in a small bay, neatly enclosed in a stretch of coastal rocks where the Castell-Cap Roig Natural Area begins and outside the centre of Calella de Palafrugell. The beach is surrounded by wooded areas, small coves and cliffs, and is accessed by following a long stairway from the El Golfet housing development. A seaside path also provides access to this beach from the centre of Calella de Palafrugell. It is flanked by the Punta dels Forcats to the east and by Cap Roig to the west, where we find the botanical garden bearing the same name. The surrounding areas of the beach, as well as the coves we find along the route of the seaside path, are ideal for diving.

This is a small, virgin cove surrounded by woods, small coves and cliffs. It is located within the Castell-Cap Roig protected natural area. Difficult to access, it can be reached on foot via the seaside path that links Castell Beach in Palamós with Calella de Palafrugell. This is the only area in Mont-ras which has open sea. It is bounded by Cape Les Planes to the south and by a small stretch of rocks to the north that leads to Cala Vedell.

This is a small virgin bay made up of small coves surrounded by woods and cliffs, which is inside the Castell-Cap Roig protected natural area. Access is gained on foot via the seaside path, which at this point resembles a forest track and links Castell Beach with Calella de Palafrugell. The Formigues Islands can be found just in front of the beach, approximately one kilometre away.

The beach is located at the southernmost point of the Castell-Cap Roig protected natural area. It is one of the few large, sandy beaches found on the Costa Brava that has not been developed, despite its proximity to the centre of Palamós. It is still practically virgin, surrounded by abundant vegetation. It is bounded by the Iberian village of Castell to the northeast and by a stretch of rocks skirted by the seaside path to the southwest, which leads to La Fosca Beach, taking in other coves along the way (s'alguer being the closest). A seaside path starts around 200 metres from the beach and takes us to Calella de Palafrugell. Other virgin beaches can be spotted as we follow this path, which takes us along the coastline.

The beach is located in a bay outside the centre of Palamós. A large black rock, which gives the place its name, splits it in two. The bay is protected by Cape Gros to the west and by Punta de Sant Esteve to the east. A seaside path starts from Punta de Sant Esteve and leads to the coves of s'alguer and El Castell.

A cove with a seafaring nature that is flanked by a row of old fishing houses which have been renovated or rebuilt as vacation homes. It is bounded to the east by Cape Gros and by a stretch of rocks to the west which leads to Cala del Morro de Vedell. A seaside path starts from the eastern side of the cove and runs along the length of Cape Gros. Not a single building can be found on this pine-covered massif. Its coastline is marked by high cliffs. In front of the beach we find some little islands, known as La Negra and, further to the left, La Figuera Borda. These are ideal for underwater diving.

A small cove hidden away behind the pleasure harbour at the Palamós Marina. The eastern part is protected by a small artificial breakwater that leads to the small islands known as Esculls d'en Roca. After this we find Cala dels Pots, which has a small stretch of very rocky beach. Different scuba diving centres carry out courses for beginners here.

It is the main beach in Palamós, located in front of the town's tourist centre. It runs between the Port of Palamós on its eastern side, which is one of the most important ports in Catalonia, and Es Monestrí Beach, in Calonge, on the western side, which is accessed via the promenade linking the two beaches together. The waves at this beach are protected by the large eastern breakwater of the port, which makes it ideal for water sports and sailing. The old centre of Palamós starts at the eastern side of the beach, just where we find the port.

The beach is located in the Bay of Palamós. The eastern side is bounded by the Platja Gran Beach, Palamós. This beach has a very special air about it: from Palamós, it looks like a green stain running from Les Gavarres. The promenade links the beach with the one in Sant Antoni by way of the bridge over the Aubi Stream. Here we can find the only club for patí català, a type of catamaran sailing, in the province of Girona.

The beach is located in the centre of Sant Antoni. It takes up a third of the Bay of Palamós and is protected by three characteristic T-shaped breakwaters (L'Amistat, El Mig and Costa Brava) and two thin, perpendicular breakwaters on the shoreline, which create small crescent-shaped coves. It is bounded by Es Monestrí Beach to the northeast and by the mouth of Torre Valentina Beach to the southwest.

This is a spacious urban beach set apart from Sant Antoni Beach by the Calonge River. An old watchtower from the 16th century can be found on this beach, which used to protect the area from pirates and now gives the beach its name. The seaside path that runs along the coast to Platja d'aro starts beside Torre Valentina Beach. The beach is located on the southernmost stretch of the Bay of Palamós.

Cove located in an area that is relatively undeveloped, with rocky terrain and vegetation. It is made up of two sections: Cristus and Ses Torretes. It is accessible by foot from the surrounding Camí de Ronda that runs between Rovita Cove and Torre Valentina and also by road.

The cove can be found at the same level as the Politur housing development. It is bounded by a stretch of rocks to the north, where we find small coves, and to the south by the Punta del Cavall Bernat, a granite monolith which is a symbol of the area and which separates it from Platja Gran Beach in Platja d'aro. A seaside path starts from the rocky point at the northern side, which follows the coastline to Torre Valentina Beach.
playas.municipio: Castell d'Aro, Platja d'Aro i s'Agaró

playas.descripcion: A long, spacious beach in the heart of the Costa Brava and located in the centre of Platja d'aro. It is bounded to the north by the Punta del Cavall Bernat, a granite monolith which has become a symbol of the area and which separates it from Cala Rovira, and by Ridaura river to the south.
playas.municipio: Castell d'Aro, Platja d'Aro i s'Agaró

playas.descripcion: The cove acts as a small bay which can be accessed via s'agaró, a town of great architectural interest. It is bounded by the rocks of Punta de Sa Conca to the south and by Punta del Pinell to the north, which links up with the Port d'Aro Marina.
playas.municipio: Castell d'Aro, Platja d'Aro i s'Agaró

playas.descripcion: This is an open half-moon shaped bay located in what is known as the Plana de Sant Pol to the east of the town centre. The street is the site of some Art Nouveau houses. It runs between two rocky areas that protect it from easterly and south-westerly winds. The beach is the site of the architectural ensemble of the former baths of S'Agaró, which are registered local cultural heritage, and the Dunes de Sant Pol, a protected dune zone.

The beach is located in the centre of town, in the heart of the Costa Brava. It runs between the port and a stretch of rocks and cliffs where small natural coves can be found. The waters of this beach are fairly well sheltered by the port jetty that protects the beach from storms.

Access can be gained via the Rosamar housing development. It is bounded by a stretch of cliffs, known as Els Esculls de Sa Bardissa, to the north and by a stretch of rocks that link up with the small Cala del Canyet, which belongs to the town of Santa Cristina d'aro, to the south. This beach is the farthest away from the town centre.

Canyet beach is a small cove located in the Rosamar urbanization, through which it is accessed. It is far from the urban center of Santa Cristina de Aro. The cove is flanked by the Punta de Canyet hill, to the east, and the Canyet reefs, to the west, linked to each other by a walkway where you can walk.

The cove is found amidst a stretch of coastal rocks and cliffs. This beach is the farthest away from the town centre. It is surrounded by a housing development that makes access by car difficult in summer, as the development is private.
The cove is found amidst a stretch of coastal rocks and cliffs in natural surroundings. It is located outside the town centre.

It is located at the northern end of the town of Tossa. It is bounded by a stretch of cliffs to the north and by a stretch of rocks to the south, leading to Tossa's Platja Gran Beach. This is considered to be the town's second beach and is well-known for the small cove found at the northern end, referred to as sa banyera de ses dones (the ladies' beach), which is an ideal bathing spot for those with children due to its shallow, calm waters.

This beach is found in the centre of town. It is bounded by a stretch of rocks to the east that leads to La Mar Menuda Beach and links up with Cape Tossa to the west. Cape Tossa and the walled enclosure of the old town create a unique silhouette and represent one of the most photographed landscapes of Tossa and the entire Costa Brava.
This small beach, which was the old fishing port of the town, is found at the foot of the old town walls, nestled between Cape Tossa and a long stretch of rocks and cliffs.

The beach can be found at the border point between Tossa de Mar and Lloret de Mar, surrounded by wooded areas and cliffs. It is made up of two coves (Llevant and Garbí) which in reality appear to be one single cove separated by rocks. They are surrounded by a residential housing development that makes access by car difficult, but access can be gained on foot.

This cove, made up of two crescents, is the farthest away from the town centre. It is bounded by a long stretch of rocks and cliffs to the east, where small coves can be found, and by a pleasure harbour to the west, which is the only marina in Lloret de Mar.
This is the longest beach in the area, and the one most frequented by tourists. It is located in the centre of town between two hills with rocky coastlines and small coves.
This is Lloret de Mar's second beach. It is located in a bay that enjoys protection from the winds thanks to a massif that separates it from the town centre and Lloret Beach.

It is hidden away between two stretches of rocks in the natural surroundings so characteristic of the Costa Brava. Access can be gained via a dirt track surrounded by leafy vegetation. Nudism is permitted.

Right in the heart of the Costa Brava, it is bounded by a stretch of rocky coastline to the north and by Cala Treumal to the south. Its location between two large hills protects it from winds and strong tides, making its waters calm and inviting. Access can be gained via a dirt track surrounded by leafy vegetation.
It is hidden away between two stretches of rocks and cliffs, well-shielded from the south-westerly winds. It is located at the foot of the residential housing development bearing the same name.

It is located in the centre of the town and runs between the port and the Sa Palomera headland, a unique rock that marks the southern starting point of the Costa Brava. On the Sa Palomera promontory a viewpoint has been established to provide an extensive view of the town and of the Tordera River delta, the mouth of which lies 2 km downstream on S'Abanell beach.

This is the longest beach in Blanes, and the one most frequented by tourists. It is bounded by the Sa Palomera rock to the north and by the mouth of the Tordera to the south, on the border of Malgrat de Mar.

playas.nombre: la Punta de la Tordera- de la Conca Beach
playas.descripcion: The beach that is bordered on the northeast by the mouth of the Tordera river that separates it from the Blanes beaches. It extends south to the beginning of the Camí de la Pomareda, which separates it from Malgrat beach. It is in a natural setting with camp sites where projects are being carried out to introduce and protect species of plants that are native to sand dune areas.  The mouth is a protected area, where nature lovers can observe a wide variety of birds and enjoy the flora of the Delta.

It is located between La Conca Beach and L'Astillero Beach, starting at the Camí de la Pomerada path and ending at the stream in Sant Genís de Palafolls. The town centre has considerable impact on this beach. The building work carried out on the Passeig de Mar, on the stretch between the stream and the street-level crossing on Carrer Abat Oiba, was completed in 1997, and the street-level crossing was replaced in 2009 by an underpass for vehicles and pedestrians.

The beach is bordered by the stream in Sant Genís de Palafolls to the northeast, which separates it from the beach in the centre of Malgrat, and by Llevant Beach in Santa Susanna to the southwest. This beach is located in front of the promenade, where we find most tourism establishments (hotels, apartments, etc.) and where most of the services and facilities offered at the beach can also be found.

The beach extends from its northeast border with Malgrat de Mar, down to the Santa Susanna river which separates it from the Les Dunes beach on its southwest border, the beach consists of a series of small coves that are separated by rocks, which the beach is named after. It is the beach where the majority of the town's hotels are located. The heart of Santa Susanna is just over one kilometer inland, while the seafront is where the town's main tourist areas are located.

The beach is located on the west side, running between the Santa Susanna Stream to the Els Pins Beach (Pineda de Mar). This beach is flanked by farmland and is home to the Santa Susanna Sailing Club, where all kinds of water sports can be enjoyed. The Mini Beach Club can also be found here, where all kinds of children's activities take place.

This is an open beach that runs from Santa Susanna Beach, to the northeast, to the Els Pescadors Beach, in the same town. The beach runs parallel to the train tracks. This beach is the farthest away from the town centre and its name refers to the small pine grove found at the beach.

It is bounded by Els Pins Beach to the northeast and the Pineda Stream to the southwest, which separates it from El Poblenou-La Riera Beach. This beach is located in front of the town centre and covers the most modern part of the residential housing development in Pineda de Mar. Most bathers gather around sailing club, located in the eastern section.

Section of linear, open beach that is located between Pescadors beach and the Rierany dels Frares, the border between Pineda de Mar and Calella. The beach runs parallel to the train tracks and is located in front of the Poblenou neighborhood.

A long beach bounded by Rierany dels Frares to the northeast, which separates it from El Poblenou Beach in Pineda de Mar, and by the Capaspre (or Calella) Stream to the southwest, separating it from Garbí Beach. This is the largest beach in Calella, located in the centre of the town, running along its seafront. Running parallel with this beach we find Passeig Manuel Puigvert, which is well known for its cultural and leisure events.

A spacious beach that runs between the Capastre Stream, which separates it from Platja Gran Beach, and the mountain of Capastre, where we find Calella Lighthouse, separating it from Les Roques Beach. This was the first beach in Catalonia to receive 'Q for Tourism Quality' certification. Located in front of the hotel zone, it is flanked by a promenade bearing the same name.

A beach made up of two small coves and located to the southeast of the town centre, at the foothills of El Montnegre i el Corredor Park and protected by the spur of Capastre mountain. A rock formation that extends into the sea and serves as a natural barrier, dividing the beach into two sections, which are accessed separately. Cliffs can be found on both sides. It is bounded by the town of Sant Pol de Mar to the southwest.

playas.nombre: La Platjola i el Morer Beach
playas.descripcion: The beach is located east of the Sant Pol de Mar town center. It is accessible from the end of Avinguda del Doctor Furet (Sant Pol de Mar promenade), or from the Roca Grossa beach, on the Calella border. At the western part, over a small breakwater, there is an observation deck that offers a panoramic view of the beach and Roca Grossa. The beach is next to the train tracks and the N-II highway.

This beach, which is also known as the Platja dels Pescadors (Fishermen¿s Beach) is located next to Sant Pol de Mar Sailing Club, in front of the town centre. To the north it is confined by a breakwater, which also separates it from Les Escaletes beach, while to the south it is delimited by the riverbed of Sant Pol, which separates it from Can Villar beach.

This broad beach is located to the south of the town centre. It is confined in the north by the riverbed of Sant Pol, next to Les Barques beach, and in the south by a small breakwater known as La Punta del Refugi ¿site of a bunker from the Spanish Civil War¿, which separates it from La Murtra beach. The beach runs parallel to the railway line.

In the northeast it is confined by a small breakwater known as La Punta del Refugi ¿site of a bunker from the Spanish Civil War¿, which separates it from Can Villar beach, and in the southwest it is delimited by a small cliff that separates it from Roques Blanques, which is the beach farthest from the town centre. The north-eastern section is formed by small sandy areas among rocks that stretch down into the sea. The beach runs parallel to the railway line and to the N-II highway. It can be reached via underpasses from the other side of the road.

This is the municipality¿s northernmost beach. In the northeast it is confined by a small cliff that separates it from La Murtra beach and in the southwest by the Oms riverbed that separates it from Canet beach. It runs parallel to the railway line and to the N-II highway An underpass by the riverbed can be used to reach the beach from the other side of the road.

A long, spacious beach bounded by the Les Roques Blanques Beach in Sant Pol de Mar to the northeast, and by a small jetty located beside the Sailing Club to the southwest, which separates it from Cavaió Beach, in Canet. This beach is located in the town centre and is flanked by a promenade, where we can find an area designated for the protection of coastline vegetation in the eastern part. Plants which are characteristic of the Catalan coastline can be found here, such as sea fennel, European searocket, yellow hornpoppy and American aloe.

A long, spacious beach bounded by a jetty to the northeast, separating it from Canet Beach, and bordered on the west by Arenys de Mar Beach in the town of the same name. Although it is not located in front of the town centre, it is located along the promenade, where interesting Art Nouveau buildings by Puig i Cadafalch, Domènech i Roure, and Domènech i Montaner, among other Art Nouveau architects, can be found. The coastline is made up of sandy beaches, the result of the decomposition of the granite rocks that make up the subsoil found in Canet.

This broad beach runs between the port of Arenys and the Vallmaria riverbed, which borders on the municipality of Canet de Mar. It is actually connected to Canet de Mar beach. It lies outside the town centre.

Also known as Primera Platja Beach or Arenys Beach, La Picòrdia Beach is located in front of the town centre, to the east of the port, between the port and Les Roques d'en Lluc Beach, level with the train station. This is where the Arenys Stream, one of the longest in El Maresme, flows into the sea.

This beach lies to the west of the town of Arenys de Mar, outside the town centre and by the seafront next to the Torre dels Encantats hill, between the Punta de Canyadell rocky outcrop and the municipal boundary with Caldes d¿Estrac.

A spacious, long and open beach located in a residential area outside the town centre. It is located between La Musclera Beach to the east and Els Tres Micos Beach to the west. It runs parallel to the promenade found in Caldes d'estrac. Its name comes from the fact that the Caldes Stream flows into the sea at this point.

This broad, open and linear beach is located in a residential zone, outside the town centre. It lies between El Kalima beach in the east and Sant Vicenç de Montalt beach in the west. The beach runs parallel to the Passeig dels Anglesos, a street with Art Nouveau houses in the style of the summer residential and spa tradition of the early twentieth century. In the same street there is a municipal thermal spa, which offers hot water and seawater treatments and services.

This broad, open and linear beach is located in a residential zone, outside the town centre, and lies between Els Tres Micos beach of Caldetes in the east and El Balís beach, to the east of Port Balís. It runs parallel to Passeig Marquès Casa Riera, which is a continuation of Els Tres Micos beach and an avenue of Art Nouveau houses in the style of the summer residential and spa tradition of the early twentieth century.

Beach located in a residential area, outside of the town center, where the train station is located. The beach is bordered on the northeast with Port Balís and on the southeast it connects to a small jetty, where there is a large breakwater separating it from Mataró. The Balís stream runs into it. It is parallel to the train tracks and the N-II highway.

It is located in surroundings which are predominately used for farming in the town of Mataró. To the southwest, it is bounded by the Sant Simó (de Valldeix) Stream, which separates it from El Callao Beach, and to the northeast by a jetty area that runs to the town of Sant Andreu de Llavaneres. A bunker dating back to the Spanish Civil War can be found at this beach.

A spacious beach which is bounded to the northeast by the Sant Simó (de Valldeix) Stream, which separates it from the beach of the same name, and to the southwest by the breakwater of the old sailing club in Mataró, which separates it from El Varador Beach. The beach is flanked by a large garden area. Access can be gained on foot via the promenade.

A spacious beach in front of the town centre. To the northeast, the beach is bounded by the breakwater of the old sailing club in Mataró, which separates it from El Callao Beach, and by the Port of Mataró to the southwest. Access can be gained on foot via the promenade.

It is bounded by a breakwater that separates it from the port area to the northeast, and by another breakwater that separates it from a jetty area that extends to Cabrera de Mar in the southwest. This is the smallest beach in Mataró and is located beside an area with a constant inflow and outflow of boats and where bathing is prohibited. The breakwaters of the port protect it from the easterly winds and keep the waves under control.

An open and linear beach located between Santa Margarida beach to the east, and Almadrava beach in Vilassar de Mar to the west. It gets wider as it goes west from Mataró. It is located outside of the town center and runs parallel to the train tracks and the N-II highway, in a residential and agricultural setting. It is accessible by car via Pas Palomares and Pas Bona Mar.

A narrow and linear beach in front of the Vilassar de Mar town center, between the Vinyals torrent, next to the train station, at the border of Cabrera de Mar, and the Garbí torrent. It runs parallel to the promenade, the train tracks and the N-II highway. Along the promenade there are interesting summer homes in the modernist-style. There are a few underground paths making it accessible by foot. At the southwest end of the beach there is another train station.

A long, narrow beach located in farming and residential surroundings, between the Garbí breakwater and the Les Tartanes torrent, which separates Llevant Beach from Premià de Mar. This is El Mercat de la Flor Beach. The beach runs parallel to the train tracks and the N-II road. There are underpasses to access the beach on foot. The train station is very close by.

It runs between the Les Tartanes torrent, near the Mercat de les Flors, which borders Vilassar de Mar, and the Port of Premià, which is to the west of the beach. It is located outside the town centre. The beach widens as we get nearer to the port. The beach runs parallel to the train tracks and the N-II road. There are underpasses to access the beach on foot.

The beach extends from the Port of Premià to the Ocata beach in Masnou and it is made up of four different sections. It is located in front of the town center. It is accessible by underground paths or from the main footpath that runs along the beach. Parallel to the beach are the train tracks and the N-II highway and in the center is the train station. The width is quite variable, depending on the height of the water and how the sand is dispersed.

A very wide, spacious beach located in front of the neighbourhood that gives the beach its name. It is bounded by Ponent Beach (Premià de Mar) to the northeast and by the Port of El Masnou to the southwest. The beach runs parallel to the train tracks and the N-II road.

It is confined in the east by the Port of El Masnou and in the west opens out onto Monsolís beach. It is not as urban as Ocata beach, as it is set farther away from the town. The railway line and the N-II highway run parallel to the beach.

This beach extends from the border with El Masnou to the rocky area that separates it from the Roques beach section, also in Montgat.  It becomes narrower the closer it gets to the Masnou beach. It is made up of four sections: Toldos, Monsolís, Can Tano and Les Barques, where the 16th century Ca n'Alzina watchtower is located, which was built as protection against pirate attacks.

Roques beach is bordered on the northeast by a rocky ridge located at the height of the Montgat hill, which separates it from the beach of Les Barques, and by the southeast with a breakwater behind which there is a large car park where there was before the former explosive factory Río Tinto.

Located in the Casagemes neighborhood, between the Montgat border and the Riera Canyadó, it gets its name because in the past, there was an important glass factory located there. It the beach furthest north in Badalona, and like the rest of the beaches in the municipality, it is located in a setting that is highly urban and industrial. It is made up of two sections: Barca Maria and Cristall.

This beach is the most central section, and it gets its name because there are boats used by the fishermen. To the northeast it borders with the Cristall beach (Canyadó river) and to the southwest, with the Coco beach (Avinguda Martí Pujol). It is where many of Badalona¿s most emblematic places are located, like the Club Nàutic Bétulo, site of the former Titus night club, and the Club Natació Badalona which attracts sailing enthusiasts. There is also a play area for children, a canal for boats, and a service providing assistance and changing rooms for reduced-mobility patrons during the beach season. Like the rest of the beaches in Badalona, it is located in a setting that is highly urban and industrial.

This beach extends from the border with the Pescadors beach to the Port of Badalona. It is made up of three sections: L'Estació, where the train station is located, El Pont de Petroli and Coco. It is located in a setting that is highly urban and industrial. Its highlights include its proximity to the Port de Badalona, and in particular, the Pont del Petroli, a pier that was built for unloading petroleum products from tankers, and in 2009, was remodeled for use by scientists and the general public. You can also find the modernist Mono factory, an emblematic building in the city, and the statue of the Mono monkey at the end of the pier.

Marina beach of the Badalona marina and fishing port is a small cove located at the west of the port and protected by the sheltered dike, which makes it have maximum stability, practically the entire year. This beach is delimited at the south by the protection breakwaters of the interceptor collector spillway and to the north by the southern contradique of the port.

The beach is in front of the park which gives the beach its name. It is bounded by the reservoir of the thermal power station to the northeast, which separates it from La Mora Beach in Badalona, and by the jetty at the mouth of the Besòs River to the southwest. It is located in highly urban and industrial surroundings.

The beach is part of the Parc de la Pau, or Peace Park, which is built next to and named in honour of the area where the Campament de la Pau, or Peace Camp, was located. In 2004, hundreds of children from areas of conflict stayed there during their 10-day visit to Barcelona as part of the Forum of Cultures. The beach is bounded by the mouth of the Besòs River to the northeast, and by Forum Port to the southwest; it is located in highly urban and industrial surroundings.

It is located within the enclosure of Barcelona Forum Park. With the photovoltaic panel of the Forum as a backdrop, this bathing area is like a seawater swimming pool in the open sea, with a very clearly designated bathing area. It is one of the most innovative and most used creations of Forum Park.

It is the last beach of those created along the Barcelona coastline, and was introduced to the city in the summer of 2006. The beach is bounded by a breakwater (which separates it from the site of the future marine zoo) to the northeast and by another breakwater to the southwest, which separates it from La Nova Mar Bella Beach.

It is part of the series of beaches that were recovered along the coastline of Barcelona as part of the urban renovation that took place for the Barcelona Olympic Games. It sits between two breakwaters: one that separates it from Llevant Beach to the northeast, and another, the Bac de Roda breakwater, which separates it from La Mar Bella Beach to the southwest.

This is one of the beaches that were created as part of the urban remodelling of the coastline that took place in 1992 for the Barcelona Olympic Games. It sits between two breakwaters: the Bac de Roda breakwater to the northeast, which separates it from La Nova Mar Bella Beach; and the El Ferrocarril breakwater to the southwest, which separates it from Bogatell Beach.

This is one of the beaches that acquired a new status when the remodelling of the Barcelona coastline took place during the nineties. It sits between two breakwaters: the El Ferrocarril breakwater to the northeast, which separates it from La Mar Bella Beach; and the Bogatell breakwater to the southwest, which separates it from La Nova Icària Beach.

This is one of the beaches located in the centre of the city coastline. Its north-eastern part is bounded by the Bogatell breakwater, which separates it from the beach bearing the same name; its south-western part is bounded by the Barcelona Olympic Port, which separates it from La Barceloneta Beach.

It could be said that, among other its other values, this beach epitomises the recovery of the historical memory. Some years ago, this stretch of coastline, along with part of La Barceloneta Beach and the beaches of La Nova Icària and Bogatell, were home to the slums known as 'Somorrostro'. It is now one of the most emblematic beaches in the city, not to mention one of the most favoured by tourists as well as leisure clubs and schools, who often use it for outings. To the northeast, the beach is bounded by the Olympic Port, which separates it from La Nova Icària Beach, while it is bounded to the southwest by the El Gas breakwater, which separates the beach from La Barceloneta Beach. Its proximity to the Olympic Port and the Port of Barcelona is also worth mentioning.

It is one of the oldest and most traditional of the city's beaches, not to mention one of the most favoured by tourists as well as leisure clubs and schools, who often use it for outings. Facing the sea, there is a raised promenade under which we find the Espai del Mar, an environmental education resource centre designed to aid access to the beach and the marine environment and to promote environmental education on the coast by increasing the inclusive practice of sport and leisure activities. La Barceloneta Beach is bounded by the El Gas breakwater to the northeast, which separates it from El Somorrostro Beach, and by Sant Miguel Beach to the southwest. Of particular note is its proximity to the Olympic Port and the Port of Barcelona.

It is located between the beaches of Sant Sebastià and La Barceloneta. Its name comes from the church in La Barceloneta (Sant Miquel del Port). Located right next to Plaça del Mar, this is one of the most visited places along the Barcelona coastline.

It is considered to be one of the oldest and most traditional beaches, alongside El Somorrostro and La Barceloneta beaches, with sports clubs that are very important to the city due to the water-related activities carried out there. Of particular note is the proximity to two important ports in the city: the Olympic Port and the Port of Barcelona. The beach is bounded by Sant Miquel Beach to the northeast and by the Port of Barcelona to the southwest.

A beach that extends southwest from the Aviació canal, at approximately 400 m wide, which varies greatly depending on regression of the coast from the previous winter, until reaching the Estany del Remolar pond. Two kilometers northeast of the beach is the mouth of the Llobregat river, which is very close to one of the runways at the Prat Airport. Further away from downtown Prat, it is entirely included within the Xarxa Natura 2000 network. It is made up of four sections: Naturista, Can Camins, Roberta and Remolar.

playas.nombre: Remolar- Pineda de Cal Francès Beach
playas.descripcion: This beach is part of the Natural Areas of the Llobregat Delta. The beach extends from the Remolar pond in the northwest, to the mouth of the Sant Climent river, in the southwest. It is an undeveloped beach, outside of the city, that has sand dunes across the entire stretch of coast and has a forest of pine trees, the Stone Pine, behind it. It is a natural, virgin beach.

This beach is part of the Natural Areas of the Llobregat Delta.  To the northeast, it borders the Sant Climent river which separated it from the La Pineda de Cal Francès beach, and to the southwest, it borders the Murtra canal, which separates it from the Estany de Gavà beach. It is located outside of Viladecans center. The stretch of beach is a protected natural area and it is included in the Xarxa Natura 2000 network.

This constitutes the northern section of Gavà beach. It is confined in the northeast by the Canal de la Murtra, which separates it from Viladecans beach. It is located in a residential area, away from the town centre.

The beach is confined in the northeast by beach of the municipal lake and in the southwest by Castelldefels¿ La Pineda beach. The beach has a unique pinewood that measures some 400 metres wide and stretches all the way to the seafront. It is a residential area, set away from the town centre.

This beach stretches between the Canyars stream to the east and the Pineda de Castelldefels beach to the west. This is a beach located in a residential area away from the town center, which is accompanied by dunes in its entirety and with a coastal pine forest, with pine trees in the background.

The beaches of Castelldefels belong to two very different natural systems: the Llobregat Delta, with its marshlands and reed beds, and the calcareous massif of El Garraf. The beach is bounded by Gavà Beach to the northeast and by Les Lluminetes Beach to the southwest.

The beaches of Castelldefels belong to two very different natural systems: the Llobregat Delta, with its marshlands and reed beds, and the calcareous massif of El Garraf. The beach is bounded by La Pineda Beach to the northeast and by El Baixador Beach to the southwest.

The beaches of Castelldefels belong to two very different natural systems: the Llobregat Delta, with its marshlands and reed beds, and the calcareous massif of El Garraf. The beach is bounded by Les Lluminetes Beach to the northeast and by Les Botigues Beach, in Sitges, to the southwest.

At a distance of 23 km, this beach is the farthest away from the town centre of Sitges. It is bounded by El Baixador Beach in Castelldefels to the northeast and by the Port Ginesta breakwater to the southwest.

It is located very near to the El Garraf massif natural area. The beach is bounded by a small cliff (Punta dels Corrals) to the northeast, and by the Port of El Garraf to the southwest. The seaside huts found on this beach, which have been declared a site of interest, are very characteristic and give the place a particularly unique appeal.

This beach is located to the east of the Aiguadolç marina, in front of the Marina d'Aiguadolç residential zone. It is confined in the northeast by an area of small cliffs and in the southwest by the breakwater and access roads to the port of Aiguadolç, which separates it from Els Balmins beach. The beach is noteworthy for the freshwater springs that rise intermittently and have given the beach its name.

A semi-urban beach without a promenade where nudism is permitted. It is bounded by the jetty of the Port of Aiguadolç (Punta Grossa) to the northeast, which separates it from Aiguadolç Beach, and by a cliff (Punta de les Mabres) to the southwest.

Right in the town centre, tucked in an old neighbourhood with a strong sailing tradition, we find Sant Sebastià Beach, bounded by the Punta de la Llengua de Serp to the northeast, and the Punta de la Torreta to the southwest. Very close to this beach we find the Cau Ferrat Museum, which was the home and study of painter, collector, journalist and Catalan Art Nouveau playwright, Santiago Rusiñol. Part of Rusiñol's work is kept in this museum, as well as pieces from other artists of the period (Utrillo, Casas, Picasso, Anglada Camarasa, etc.). We also find furniture and artefacts made of iron, pottery, glass, etc., which Rusiñol collected throughout his life.

It is one of the most popular, frequented and cosmopolitan beaches thanks to its location in the very heart of Sitges. It is bounded by a jetty to the northeast, which separates it from La Fragata Beach, and by another to the southwest, which separates it from L'Estanyol Beach.

Located in front of the residential area of Vinyet. l'estanyol Beach is bounded by a jetty to the east, which separates it from La Bassa Rodona Beach, and by another jetty to the west which separates it from La Riera Xica Beach.

Located in front of the residential sector of the garden-city of Terramar. One of its unique features are the four artificial islands created to protect the sand. The beach is bounded by a jetty to the east, which separates it from La Riera Xica Beach. To the west, it is bounded by a T-shaped jetty that separates it from Terramar Beach.

Located in front of the residential sector of the garden-city of Terramar. One of its unique features are the four artificial islands created to protect the sand. To the east, it is bounded by a T-shaped jetty that separates it from La Barra Beach. To the west, it is bounded by another T-shaped jetty called Punta de les Anquines.

playas.nombre: El Far de Sant Cristòfol Beach
playas.descripcion: A spacious beach bounded by Punta Mabrera to the north, where a rocky stretch of coastline starts and continues on until Sitges. It is located outside the centre. A stretch of the extensive GR-92 trail, which takes us all the way to Sitges along the coastline, leaves from this beach. The beach can be identified by the two emblematic elements found there: the lighthouse and the shrine of Sant Cristòfol. The former is now the home to the Museu del Mar (Seafarers' Museum), with a permanent exhibition on fishermen, their origins and their working tools. The shrine of Sant Cristòfol is found above the promenade. Beside it we find the house which was home to writer Eugeni d'ors, one of the most prominent names in Catalan literature.

A spacious and popular crescent-shaped beach which is bounded by the port to the north and by Adarró Beach to the south. It is the closest to the town centre. Both beaches are separated by a T-shaped jetty on which we find a sculpture dedicated to Pasiphaë, a Greek goddess and mother of the Minotaur, who is the icon of this beach. Facing the sea we find Ribes Roges Park, a green area with many trees and gardens. Within the park there is a track of miniature trains that both young and old can take a ride on.

A spacious crescent-shaped beach bounded by Ribes Roges Beach to the east. Both beaches are separated by a T-shaped jetty, where we find a sculpture dedicated to Pasiphaë, a Greek Goddess and mother of the Minotaur. Located in residential surroundings. Bounded by Sant Gervasi Beach to the southwest, which it is separated from by a small breakwater. The beach is in front of the remains of the Iberian site that gives the beach its name.

A small and peaceful crescent-shaped beach. It is protected by two breakwaters that separate it from Adarró Beach to the northeast and from a small stretch of rocks that lead to Punta de Santa Llucía to the south. The beach is adjacent to two of the most emblematic buildings in Vilanova: Xalet del Nin and the shrine of Sant Gervasi. Both of them are within the walled enclosure. The Xalet is located within the old defence tower and fort. The shrine, built in 1566, is very close by and is dedicated to Saint Gervasi and Saint Protasi, defenders of the whole area against disease, according to legend.

Ibersol Beach is bounded to the northeast by Platja Llarga Beach and to the southwest by another beach by the same name, but in the town of Cubelles. The Santa Maria torrent separates the two towns. It is protected from storms by the three T-shaped breakwaters that divide it into two crescent-shaped beaches. It is located within residential surroundings and is the farthest from the centre of Vilanova i la Geltrú.

Platja Llarga Beach is bounded to the northeast by Ibersol Beach, which belongs to Vilanova i la Geltrú, while to the southwest it is bounded by a breakwater that separates it from the mouth of the Foix River. It is protected by three breakwaters that divide it into two crescent-shaped coves. It is located in residential surroundings outside the town centre. At the mouth of the Foix River we find a natural area of considerable ecological value. The mouth of the river is separated from the sea by a sand barrier formed by different currents that have created freshwater lagoons.

playas.nombre: la Mota de Sant Pere Beach
playas.descripcion: A long beach, bounded by the mouth of the Foix River to the northeast and by the discharge canal of the Foix thermal power station to the southwest. It is located in residential surroundings outside the town centre. At the mouth of the Foix River we find a natural area of considerable ecological value. The mouth of the river is separated from the sea by a sand barrier, Punta de Sant Pere, formed by different currents that have created freshwater lagoons.

A small beach protected by breakwaters, bounded by the discharge canal of the Foix thermal power station to the north and the Port of Cubelles to the south. It is located in residential surroundings outside the town centre.

A semi-circular cove shared with the town of Cunit. The Mas d'en Pedro Stream splits the cove in two. The northern section belongs to Cubelles and the southern to Cunit. The beach is bounded by the Port of Cubelles to the northeast.

The beach is confined in the northeast by the Mas d'en Pedro riverbed that separates it from Les Gavines de Cubelles beach. It stretches south-westwards to form a series of semi-circular coves separated by 4 breakwaters. It is located in a residential area.
A long beach formed by successive semi-circular coves separated by three T-shaped breakwaters. In the southwest it borders on Calafell. It is located in a residential area, outside the town centre.

Wide and long linear beach bordering the municipality of Cunit to the east and the port of Segur-Calafell to the west. It coincides with the sea front of the Segur de Calafell core and is flanked by a long promenade that connects the beaches of the town.

Wide and long linear beach bordering the port of Segur-Calafell to the east and Estany Mas-Mel beach to the west. It coincides with the sea front of the Segur de Calafell core and is flanked by a long promenade that connects the beaches of the municipality.

A long, spacious beach that borders with Segur de Calafell Beach to the east and with Calafell Beach to the west. It links up with the waterfront of Segur de Calafell and is flanked by a long promenade that connects the town's three beaches. Nearby, we find the archaeological site of the old Iberian city of Toixoneres.

A long, spacious beach that borders with l'estany-Mas Mel Beach to the east and with Sant Salvador Beach to the west. It is at the centre of the town's waterfront, and is flanked by a long promenade that connects the town's three beaches.

The beach is bounded by Calafell Beach to the northeast and by Coma-ruga Beach (El Vendrell) to the southwest. We find the Bisbal Stream in the middle of the bathing area. We find an ancient shrine at this beach which is considered to be the oldest building in the town. At the southern part of the beach we find the Pau Casals House-Museum Foundation, which was the old summer home of this important figure in Catalan and international music in the 20th century, and where concerts, conferences, guided visits, night-time visits, etc., are now held and whose purpose is to promote and disseminate music and culture.

The beach of Coma-ruga Llevant borders on the northeast with the beach of Sant Salvador of the same municipality and on the southwest with the port of Coma-ruga. It is flanked by a long pedestrian promenade that connects the beaches of the municipality.

The beach of Coma-ruga Ponent borders on the south-west with the beach of Francàs and on the north-east, with the port of Coma-ruga. On this beach is "el Riuet", which is the mouth of the warm thermal waters that spontaneously emerge on the surface from the pond located in the urban center of Coma-ruga. In the extreme southwest, part of the bathing area is part of the marine reserve of Masia Blanca. The beach is flanked by a long promenade that connects the beaches of the municipality.

El Francàs Beach is bounded by Coma-ruga Beach to the northeast and by Costa Daurada Beach (Roda de Barà) to the southwest. On the north-western side, part of the beach belongs to the Masia Blanca marine reserve.

A long, spacious beach that runs between El Francàs Beach in El Vendrell and the eastern breakwater of the pleasure harbour in Roda de Berà. Far from the town centre, the beach is located in front of the residential housing development bearing the same name. The beach widens as we get nearer to the port.

A small beach nestled between the eastern breakwater of the Roda de Berà pleasure harbour and the stretch of rocks that form the Punta del Roc de Sant Gaietà, which protect the beach from storms. Located away from the town centre, it is found at the foot of the Roc de Sant Gaietà housing development, comprised of typically Mediterranean houses, nestled within a natural rock formation that extends into the sea.

A small, narrow beach nestled between the breakwater of the jetty of Roc de Sant Gaietà to the east, and a stretch of rocks that separate it from Platja Llarga Beach, in Roda de Barà, to the west. It is flanked by a small pine grove which protects the rear of the beach. Located away from the town centre, it is found at the foot of the Roc de Sant Gaietà housing development, comprised of typically Mediterranean houses, nestled within the natural rock formation known as the Punta del Roc de Sant Gaietà, which extends into the sea.

A long, spacious beach that runs between a small stretch of rocks to the northeast and Creixell Beach to the southwest, with which it is connected. We find a small dune area, which is the result of the different measures taken in the town to preserve the ecosystem found here. The beach runs parallel to the train tracks, at a distance from the town centre, in residential surroundings where we also find campsites. At the top of the hill, formed by a stretch of rocks to the northeast and running along the sea, we find a Baroque-style shrine known as Mare de Déu de Berà. Leaving the beach behind and going inland, we find the Arc de Berà, a triumphal arch from the Roman era built on the old Via Augusta.

A long, spacious beach that runs between the beaches of Roda de Barà and Torredembarra, which it links together, and along the entire coastline of the town. The beach is located in a residential area with campsites outside the town centre. To the far southeast, there is the Els Salats i Muntanyans Area of Natural Interest, an area of dunes and marshlands of great ecologic value, which it shares with Torredembarra.

A long, spacious beach that runs between the beaches of Creixell and El Barri Marítim, which it links together. Included within the Plan for Areas of Natural Interest (PEIN), Els Salats i Muntanyans is home to a unique ecosystem of considerable value in terms of landscape and ecology and is made up of semi-mobile dunes and salty lagoons.

A long, spacious beach that runs between the beaches of Els Muntanyans and La Paella, it is also known as Baix a Mar. It is located in front of the old fishing area, between the sailing club and Plaça de Narcís Monturiol. At the end of the beach we find the environmental education centre of Cal Bofill, which pays homage to the doctor who was twice mayor of the town. As well as being a valuable Art Nouveau heritage site, this space is now used to raise environmental awareness and to conserve the marine landscape.

A wide beach located between El Barri Marítim Beach and the Port of Torredembarra in a residential area. It is protected from the south-westerly winds by the port breakwater. To the west of the beach we find the hills of Els Munts, from where we can enjoy views of the coast that extend from El Garraf to the Ebro Delta and where we also find the Roman town of Els Munts, a site dating back to the 1st-2nd centuries AD. Among the remains found here, the thermal baths are of particular interest, as they are considered to be the largest private baths of this kind in Catalonia.

A small cove nestled in a row of cliffs known as El Roquer, which have been eroded by the sea shared by Alatafulla and Torredembarra and are made up of bare rock and Mediterranean vegetation. The last lighthouse to be built in Spain can be found along these cliffs, which can be crossed on foot. The north-western third of the beach belongs to the town of Altafulla.

A long, spacious beach bounded to the northeast by a stretch of rocks, El Roquer, leading to Torredembarra, and to the southwest by Tamarit Beach. The Gaià River, the town border, separates both beaches. It is located in front of Les Botigues de Mar, a neighbourhood in the town of Altafulla which is protected as a site of local cultural interest, built in the 18th century as a result of the economic progress brought about by the town's maritime trade. The area around the mouth of the Gaià River mouth was declared a wildlife nature reserve in 1995.

A long beach bounded by Altafulla Beach to the northeast. The Gaià River, the town border, separates both beaches. It is bound to the west by an area of low cliffs that lead to Punta de la Mora. The area around the mouth of the Gaià River is an area of high ecological interest that was declared a wildlife nature reserve in 1995. The row of cliffs to the west of the beach is part of the natural area of Tamarit-Punta de la Móra, a number of hectares of which belong to the marine reserve. Close to this beach we find the medieval castle of Tamarit, which dates back to the 11th century, and whose current building was constructed between the 16th and 18th centuries and restored in 1916.

A spacious cove found in the centre of the natural area of Tamarit-Punta de la Móra, which the beach and its surroundings belong to, as do a number of hectares of the marine reserve. It is located in front of the residential housing development of the same name, amidst cliffs that make up the natural are and that extend to Tamarit to the east and to Roca Plana to the west. Along this stretch we find the Torre de la Móra, a defence tower from the 16th century, used to alert inhabitants in the event of pirate attacks.

Llarga Beach is divided into two sections due to its size. The northernmost section is part of the Tamarit-Punta de la Móra natural area. The beach is located far from the main city of Tarragona, in a residential setting with camp sites. In the back there is a narrow strip of almost uninterrupted dunes. Close to this beach, headed away from the sea, is Scipio's tower, a Roman funerary monument from the 1st century A.D., which is nine meters tall, located on Via Augusta road.

A cove tucked away among the low rock formations that run between Punta de la Savinosa and Punta de l'arrabassada. It is located outside the town centre, surrounded by low rocks covered with vegetation in a residential area. The train tracks runs parallel to the beach and can be accessed via an underpass.

A spacious cove bounded by low rock formations that run between Punta de l'arrabassada and Punta Grossa. Close to the city centre of Tarragona, this is a very popular beach located in a residential area. The beach runs parallel to the train tracks.

The beach is bounded by a rock formation known as the Punta del Miracle to the northeast and by  the Tarragona pleasure harbour to the southwest. Located at the base of the city centre, this is one of the most popular beaches. It is located at the cliff known as the Balcó del Mediterrani, very close to the old town. Visitors can admire the splendour of the old Roman Tarraco (the beach is very close to the Roman circus and Praetorium). Right next to the beach we find the Roman amphitheatre from the 2nd century AD, where gladiator and animal fights as well as public executions were held, and where we can also find the remains of a Visigoth basilica from the 6th century, which commemorated the martyrdom of Saint Fructuosos of Tarragona, executed in the 3rd century in this very spot. The beach runs parallel to the train tracks.

A long beach that runs northeast to the breakwater that separates it from Els Prats Beach and southwest to El Racó Beach. Located outside the centre of Vila-seca, it is within a residential area full of leisure establishments. A promenade can be found along the beach with a small pine grove in the centre that gives the beach its name. The Port of Tarragona can be seen from the beach.

This is the western part of La Pineda Beach. It is bounded to the southwest by Punta Prima, a rocky formation where Cape Salou starts. On this beach we find La Sèquia Major, a protected natural area under the Plan for Areas of Natural Interest of Catalonia (PEIN). This is a coastal wetland. Most of this area belongs to the Recreational Tourism Centre of Vila-seca and Salou. The industrial port of Tarragona can be seen from the beach.

A small cove nestled between cliffs that form Cape Salou, on the stretch that runs from Punta del Cavall to the lighthouse, which it is very close to. It is located outside the centre in a residential area. This cove and the others in the area can be accessed by the roads leading off the main coastal road or on foot via the paths that follow the coastline.

A small cove nestled between cliffs that form Cape Salou, on the stretch that runs from Punta del Cavall to Punta dels Replanells. It is located in an area of residential apartments outside the town centre. This cove and the others in the area can be accessed by the roads leading off the main coastal road or on foot via the paths that follow the coastline.

It is the largest beach found in the Cape Salou area. It can be found among the cliffs in the stretch that runs from Punta dels Replanells to Punta Purroig. Flanked on both sides by hotel buildings and residential areas, the rear part is surrounded by pine groves. A promenade runs parallel to the beach. Removed from the tourist areas, which makes it less populated than other beaches in the town. There is a small area of dunes where efforts are made to promote the regeneration of the coastal vegetation and to raise awareness of the importance of conserving coastal ecosystems among the local population as well as visitors.

A small, spacious cove nestled between two rocky tips: Punta de Purroig and Punta de les Ferreries. It is located in a residential area of apartment blocks, outside the town centre. At the top of the beach we find a small park, with terraced rocks leading to it. There is a monument to remind us that this is the point from where James I of Aragon's ships set sail to conquer Majorca.

This is the longest beach in Salou. It is bounded to the east by the rocky formation of Els Pilons and to the southwest by the breakwater of the Salou pleasure harbour. The beach is in the centre of town and is one of the most populated in Catalonia, offering a wide variety of services and leisure facilities. A wide, landscaped promenade runs parallel to the beach.

A long beach that is bounded to the northeast by the Salou pleasure harbour, which separates it from Llevant Beach, and by Cap de Sant Pere Beach, Cambrils, to the southwest. Close to the town centre, it is located in a residential area with apartment blocks. The Barenys Ravine flows into this beach.

Located in the eastern part of the coast of Cambrils, it runs between Ponent Beach, in Salou, to Vilafortuny Beach, in Cambrils. A breakwater running parallel to the coast which prevents the erosion of the beach separates it from the adjacent beaches. It is located in a residential area outside the town centre. Close by we find Vilafortuny Castle, built in the 12th century and designated a Cultural Asset of Natural Interest.

A long, open beach that runs between the beaches of Cap de Sant Pere, to the east, and l'esquirol, to the west, linking them. Its name comes from the housing development adjacent to it. It is located in a residential area outside the town centre. A long promenade runs along the beach from l'esquirol to Salou. Close by we find Vilafortuny Castle, built in the 12th century and designated a Cultural Asset of Natural Interest.

l'esquirol Beach is located at the westernmost point of the stretch of sand that starts at the Maspujols Stream in Cambrils and ends at Salou Beach. It is located between a breakwater that separates it from the stream and Vilafortuny Beach, outside the town centre in a residential area. A long promenade runs along the beach and links it with the adjacent ones. Near to the beach we find the Torre de l'esquirol, a very important tower during the time when messages were sent by telegraph, as it served as a link between Madrid and La Jonquera. It is because of this that it is also known as the telegraph tower.

A long beach bounded to the northeast by a breakwater that separates it from the l'esquirol Beach, and to the southwest by another breakwater that separates it from El Prat d'en Forés Beach. It is protected by a total of 3 breakwaters that divide it into two coves. It is located in residential surroundings outside the town centre. The Riudoms, or Maspujols, Stream flows into it at this point, where we find wetlands that conserve the ecosystems typical of this environment: lagoons and reed, rush and salt cedar beds.

A long and extensive beach also known El Regueral, as the ravine bearing the same name flows into the sea at this point. The beach runs between a breakwater, which separates it from Cavet Beach to the east, and the port. It is the closest to the town centre of Cambrils. Close to the beach and within the port we find the port tower, an old watchtower that has become one of Cambrils' most emblematic monuments.

A small beach found to the west of the port which is located between the port and the Alforja Stream. Close to the centre of Cambrils, it is flanked by a wooded park and a promenade. Close to the beach and within the port we find the port tower, an old watchtower that has become one of the most emblematic monuments in Cambrils.

The eastern half of the first set of semi-circular coves that are found to the west of the port in Cambrils. The cove is divided by Mare de Déu del Camí Ravine, which separates it from La Llosa Beach. Located in a residential area. A promenade runs along the beach, linking it with the adjacent beaches. We find the Roman remains of La Llosa very close by.

A beach to the west of the port that runs between the Mare de Déu del Camí Ravine, which separates it from Horta de Santa Maria Beach, and the En Gener torrent, which separates it from Ardíaca Beach. It is made up of semi-circular coves separated by T-shaped breakwaters. In the centre of each of the coves we find small artificial islands. A promenade runs along the beach, linking it with the adjacent beaches. It is located in front of the neighbourhood of La Llosa, in a residential area.

A beach to the west of the port that runs between the En Gener torrent, which separates it from La Llosa Beach, and the Riudecanyes Stream, which separates it from Mont-roig del Camp. It is made up of semi-circular coves separated by T-shaped breakwaters. In the centre of each of the coves we find small artificial islands. A long promenade runs along the beach and links it with the adjacent ones. It is located in a residential area in front of housing developments and apartment blocks.

A long beach bounded to the east by Riudecanyes Beach, which reaches Cambrils, and to the west by the Rifà torrent. Located outside the town centre, it is found within an area of campsites and farmland. The Pixerota torrent flows into this beach and also gives it its name. A small natural site can be found to the rear of the stream. To Joan Miró, who painted it in various works, the beach "has a great beauty, very stimulating for me. Being on the beach and looking at the mountains you see very impressive pointy shapes"

A long beach that runs between Punta de Rifà to the east, which separates it from La Pixerota Beach, and Punta de la Porquerola to the west, which separates it from La Casa dels Lladres Beach. A ravine runs into the sea at both ends; La Porquerola, to the west, gives the beach its name. Located away from the town centre, it is found in a popular camping area. On the beach we find the Torre de Porquerola, a medieval fort in an excellent state of conservation that was subsequently turned into the telegraph tower.

A long beach that runs between Punta de la Porquerola to the east, which separates it from La Porquerola Beach, and Punta dels Penyals to the west, which separates it from Els Espenyals Beach. Located away from the town centre, it is found in a residential area with campsites. In the centre of this beach we find a Mediterranean lagoon known as L'Estany Gelat, a protected natural area which was included in the Natura Network in 2000.

A stretch of beach bounded by Punta dels Penyals to the east and by a rock formation, with cliffs dotted with small coves, to the west, which runs along the coastline to Cristall Beach. Far from the town centre, it is located in a residential area with apartment blocks. Sheltered by a pine grove, the beach is surrounded by low-lying cliffs that divide it in two, Els Espenyals to the northeast and Cala dels Vienesos to the southwest.

A large beach bounded by calcareous cliffs to the northeast and by the mouth of the Llastres River to the southwest, which separates it from the town of Vandellòs i l'Hospitalet de l'infant. Located away from the town centre, it is found in a residential area. The beach is flanked by a promenade that links it to Punta del Riu Beach in Vandellòs i l'Hospitalet de l'infant. The Llastres River is a natural site included in the Inventory of Wetlands in Catalonia.

This beach is located between the breakwater of the port of L¿Hospitalet de l¿Infant in the west and Llastres River in the east, on the boundary with Mont-roig del Camp. The river mouth forms a small delta and wetlands, which constitute an area of natural interest and are registered in the Inventory of Wetlands of Catalonia. It is home to protected habitats and species such as the Spanish toothcarp and the tamarellar. The beach is close to the town centre.

It is the municipality¿s longest beach and runs between L'Hospitalet de l'Infant-Vandellòs marina in the east and the head of Cala d¿Oques in the west. The north-eastern section lies within the town centre. Towards the west the surroundings are residential and there is a spacious gardened seafront. The Costa Daurada Nautical Base, which offers a broad range of water sports, lies in front of L'Arenal beach.

Natural beach confined naturally at both ends by rocks. It is located in La Rojala Area of Natural Interest, which is characterised by the presence of dunes, shrubs and pines and home to fascinating species such as the sea daffodil and Bonelli¿s eagle. It is a major nudist destination and located next to a nudist camp site. At the western end there is a promontory known as La Illeta del Torn. It is a rocky outcrop upon which there are still vestiges of a watchtower. The beach is relatively isolated and set away from the town centre. It can be reached on the N-340 highway, which affords pleasant views.

A long beach that runs from a low rocky area in the northwest of the Cap del Terme riverbed, which is natural boundary with L¿Ametlla de Mar, where the Barranc de les Forques flows into the sea. It is located in a small fishing town of white houses that goes by the same name and was established in the nineteen-twenties. Its name comes from the nets that were used at the time to catch migratory fish. It is the beach farthest away from the towns of Vandellòs and L¿Hospitalet de l¿Infant.
