A small, U-shaped cove which is naturally bounded on both sides by a row of cliffs dotted with small coves that run between l'ametlla de Mar and l'ampolla. Its natural surroundings are of particular interest in terms of landscape and are part of the protected ecosystem known as the Plana de Sant Jordi. This beach is the farthest away from the town centre.

A small cove which is naturally bounded on both sides by the row of cliffs dotted with small coves that run between l'ametlla de Mar and l'ampolla. The area around the coves is of considerable interest both in terms of its ecological value and its cultural heritage. The cove is part of the Plana de Sant Jordi, a protected natural area that boasts a variety of flora and fauna unique to this landscape. The beach also houses Sant Jordi d'alfama Castle, the headquarters of the military order of Sant Jordi d'alfama, which dates back to the 14th century and which is one of the unique heritage sites in the town.

A small, U-shaped cove which is naturally bounded on both sides by a row of cliffs dotted with small coves that run between l'ametlla de Mar and l'ampolla. It is located in a residential and natural area, at a good distance from the town centre of l'ametlla. In addition to the natural interest of its surroundings, which are almost entirely covered with pine groves, Cala Forn also enjoys another attraction in terms of landscape and heritage: it is located in the area dominated by the remains of Sant Jordi d'alfama Castle, dating back to the 14th century, and a fort built during the same period.

A small, U-shaped cove which is naturally bounded on both sides by a row of cliffs dotted with small coves that run between l'ametlla de Mar and l'ampolla. It is very close to the town centre, in front of a campsite.

A small beach located just in front of the town centre of l'ametlla de Mar, beside the eastern side of the town's fishing wharf and pleasure harbour. Protected by two small stone breakwaters and flanked by a palm-lined promenade. A seaside path starts at this beach and enables visitors to explore the eastern coves of the town.

A small beach bounded by the natural port of l'estany Gros to the east and by a stretch of rocks to the west. It is located within one of the longest parts of the coastline, in an old natural port, where fishermen moored their boats until the new port was built in the 1920s. This natural park now has elements of considerable ecological value, such as the mouth of the ravine: it has a vast array of vegetation which is unique to the area, including pine groves, kermes oak trees, Mediterranean dwarf palm and other species. A seaside path starts at this beach and enables visitors to explore the western coves of the town, from El Perelló to l'ampolla.

A small cove which is naturally bounded on both sides by a row of cliffs dotted with small coves that run between l'ametlla de Mar and l'ampolla. It is located at the border of l'ametlla de Mar, to the west of Punta de l'àliga, a small peninsula which conserves the tower bearing the same name. The watchtower was built in 1598 and later turned into an observatory. The cove is in natural surroundings, quite isolated from the town centre, although the train tracks and the motorway run parallel to the cove. It can be accessed on foot via the seaside path that runs along the cliffs, or through an underground tunnel.

This is the longest beach in the town of El Perelló. It is bounded by a stretch of rocks to the east and by El Morro de Gos Beach to the west. It is the most popular beach in El Perelló, even though it is some distance from the town centre. It is surrounded by a housing development, woods and farmland.
The Morro de Gos beach is the continuation south of the Santa Llúcia beach, which is separated by a natural rock. At the southern end ends at a breakwater.

A small cove bounded naturally by red rocks from side to side; the cliffs extend out to the west to form Cape Roig. The cove is a fair distance from the town centre of El Perelló, located in a residential and tourist area.
A cove bounded by red, low-lying rocks on both sides. It is located outside the town centre of l'ampolla, to the far northeast, flanked by pine trees in a residential and tourist area.

A small beach close to the town centre, just to the east of the l'ampolla fishing wharf and pleasure harbour. The cove is flanked by a breakwater to the west and by a jetty to the east, behind which we find Els Capellans Beach. Above these rocks we find a viewpoint offering views over the whole coast.

A spacious beach that marks the beginning of the Ebro Delta. Bounded to the east by Sant Pere Ravine, where we find a mussel farm, it extends into a large sandy area to the west which forms part of the El Delta de l'ebre Natural Park. Very close to the beach we find the Les Olles pond, the smallest lagoon found in the delta. The landscape of l'arenal Beach enables visitors to distinguish between the area's own ecosystem and that of the El Delta de l'ebre Natural Park. First we find the areas that are home to the tiger nut (chufa) and reed beds, and a little further south we find the typical rice fields of the mouth of the Ebro. Right in front of the beach we find the Punta del Fangar, the Ebro Delta peninsula which, immersed in the sea, shows us one of the possible combinations of sand and dune, home to numerous species of water birds.

A beach of considerable interest for its landscape and natural heritage which forms part of the El Delta de l'ebre Natural Park, alongside the other beaches found in the Ebro Delta. It is surrounded by farmland and is bounded by the entrance to the Punta del Fangar to the northeast and by the mouth of the L'Estela pond to the southeast.

A virgin beach enjoying space and tranquillity that is part of the El Delta de l'ebre Natural Park. This is an open beach that is bounded by the L'Estela canal to the northeast and by Riumar Beach to the southeast. To the southeast, it is also worth noting its proximity to the mouth of the Ebro River.

The beach is part of the El Delta de l'ebre Natural Park. At the south-eastern part of the beach we find an area of dunes called Garxal (marshland area), while the north-eastern side of the beach is bounded by La Bassa de l'arena Beach. Near to the south-eastern side of the beach it is worth noting the mouth of the Ebro River and the fishing wharf of the Ebro Delta, which is located in the final stretch of the river.

The beach is part of the El Delta de l'ebre Natural Park. Here, the natural area is made up of El Migjorn Beach and L'Alfacada lake, which is located at the rear. Parallel to the coastline we find an area of dunes. The beach is bounded by the mouth of the inlet known as La Gola de Migjorn and Buda Beach to the northeast, and by the canal of L'Alfacada lake to the southeast. In the northeast, it is also worth nothing its proximity to the mouth of the Ebro River and the fishing wharf of the Ebro Delta, which is located in the final stretch of the river. The space and tranquillity of these areas make them the ideal place for relaxing and enjoying nature.

The beach is part of the El Delta de l'ebre Natural Park. Here the natural area is reduced to the width of the beach. An area of dunes can be found at the rear. The beach is bounded by the canal of L'Alfacada lake to the northeast and by La Platjola canal to the southeast. Above La Platjola canal and near to the beach we find La Platjola lagoon, with 61 hectares and its peculiarly long shape. The space and tranquillity of these areas make them the ideal place for relaxing and enjoying nature.

The beach lies within the Ebro Delta Natural Park. In this zone, the natural area is limited to the breadth of the beach and to La Tancada lake and La Platjola wetlands. There is an area of dunes at the rear of the beach, which is confined in the northeast by the Canal de la Platjola and in the southeast by the Poblenou del Delta road. The spaciousness of the region and the peacefulness of the surroundings make it an ideal place in which to relax and to enjoy nature.

The beach is part of the El Delta de l'ebre Natural Park. A long, narrow, bar-shaped beach with a small area of dunes to the rear, which extends to the peninsula of La Banya. This area of dunes separates El Trabucador Beach, facing the open sea, from l'aluet Beach, inside Els Alfacs Bay. The beach is one of the most unique areas in the delta and an example of the tranquillity that dominates the coastline of Les Terres de l'Ebre. Furthermore, El Trabucador Beach is also an ideal place for practicing kitesurf and windsurfing thanks to the wind that blows here in the afternoons.

The beach is part of the El Delta de l'ebre Natural Park. It is narrow, long and bar-shaped, with a small area of dunes to the rear. This area of dunes separates L'Aluet Beach from El Trabucador Beach; while El Trabucador faces the open sea, L'Aluet faces towards Els Alfacs Bay and therefore benefits from calmer waters.

The beach is bounded by the Port of Sant Carles to the northeast and by another breakwater to the southeast, which separates it from Juanito Beach. Views over Els Alfacs Bay can be enjoyed from this beach, with the profile of Punta de la Banya in the background.
A beach located very near to the town centre. It is closed in and bounded by breakwaters on each side.

It is a triangular-shaped beach just in front of the cement factory that makes use of the calcareous rocks of the mountains of El Montsià. The rear part borders the N-340 road. The main breakwater of the factory port can be found to the east, and another breakwater can be found to the west, which separates it from Maricel Beach.

The beach is very close to the N-340 road and is bounded and protected by a breakwater to the northeast and by a natural stretch of rocks to the southeast. It is located around 2 km from the maritime town of Les Cases d'alcanar.

This beach is open to the sea and runs from the port of Les Cases d'Alcanar in the north to the beaches of El Camaril in the south. The northernmost section is in the coastal district of Les Cases d'Alcanar, some 4 km from the town of Alcanar. The rest of the beach surrounds the former saltpans and reed ponds.

The bathing area is located in a natural, mountainous environment, at the town of Conca de Dalt. The Sant Antoni reservoir, also called Talarn, is a reservoir that belongs to the Noguera Pallaresa river. It is created by a dam located in the strait of Susterris, in the municipality of Talarn, and it extends through the towns of Pobla de Segur, Salàs de Pallars, Conca de Dalt, Talarn, Isona and Conca Dellà, in the county of El Pallars Jussà.

The bathing area is located in a natural, mountainous environment, in the municipality of Salàs de Pallars. The Sant Antoni reservoir also called Talarn is a reservoir that belongs to the Noguera Pallaresa river. It is created by a dam located in the Straits of Susterris, in the municipality of Talarn, it extends through the towns of Pobla de Segur, Salàs de Pallars, Conca de Dalt, Talarn and Isona and Conca Dellà, in the region of Pallars Jussà .

The bathing area is located in a natural, mountainous environment, in the town of Talarn. The Sant Antoni reservoir, also called Talarn, is a reservoir that belongs to the Noguera Pallaresa river. It is created by a dam located in the strait of Susterris, in the municipality of Talarn, and it extends through the towns of Pobla de Segur, Salàs de Pallars, Conca de Dalt, Talarn, Isona and Conca Dellà, in the county of El Pallars Jussà.

The bathing area is located in a natural, mountainous environment, in the municipality of Camarasa. The beach (50 meters long and 20 meters wide) extends along a recreational area on the left bank of the River Segre, just before reaching the municipality of Camarasa.

The reservoir of La Torrassa is a reservoir that belongs to the Noguera Pallaresa river, created by a dam between the municipalities of La Guingueta d'Àneu and Espot, which extends over its municipalities, in the county of Pallars Sobirà. The name of "la Torrassa", comes from the old and big watch tower that existed in this place. It is surrounded by paths suitable for cycling, hiking and fishing, as well as horseback excursions around the reservoir. There are also facilities for practicing nautical sports, adventure and calm waters.

The Darnius- Boadella reservoir belongs to the Muga River and is formed by a dam located in the municipality of Darnius. The bathing area is located in a natural, mountainous environment, in the same municipality. The reservoir is also extended by the terms of Sant Llorenç de la Muga, Terrades and Maçanet de Cabrenys.
Banyoles lake is the largest natural lake in Catalonia. This bathing area is part of the Banyan Swimming Club, with sports facilities that have various services.

Banyoles Lake is the largest natural lake in Catalonia. This bathing area is natural and is located in the northeastern part of the lake of Banyoles.
It is accessed through the path that goes round the lake. This way you can reach it by foot or by bike. The nearest parking lot to leave the car is in the Parc de la Draga.

The reservoir of Sant Ponç is located in the middle valley of the Cardener river, created by a dam that is near the bathing area. The marsh extends through the terms of Clariana de Cardener, Olius and Navès, in the region of Solsonès, and is part of the set of reservoirs in the river Llobregat basin. It is located in a natural, mountainous environment, in the municipality of Clariana from Cardener.

The bathing area is located in a natural, mountainous environment, in the municipality of Vilada. The Baells reservoir belongs to the Llobregat and Merdançol rivers and is formed by a dam located in the municipality of Cercs. The marsh was built between 1973 and 1976.

The bathing area is located in a natural, mountainous environment, in the municipality of Vilanova de Sau. Sau reservoir belongs to the Ter river and is formed by a dam located in the municipality of Vilanova de Sau. It is located at the foot of the Guilleries mountain range and extends through the towns of Vilanova de Sau, Les Masies de Roda, Tavertet and Santa Maria de Corcó, in the Osona region.

The bathing area is located in a natural, mountainous environment, in the municipality of Vilanova de Sau. Sau reservoir belongs to the Ter river and is formed by a dam located in the municipality of Vilanova de Sau. It is located at the foot of the Guilleries mountain range and extends through the towns of Vilanova de Sau, Les Masies de Roda, Tavertet and Santa Maria de Corcó, in the Osona region.

The bathing area is located in a natural, mountainous environment, in the municipality of Cornudella de Montsant. The Siurana reservoir belongs to the Siurana river, created by a dam located in the municipality of Cornudella de Montsant, under the Siurana cliff, which extends through its municipal district, in the Priorat region.
